newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares retrench after days of gains.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares retrench after days of gains.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Wednesday in a market taking a breather on top of two days with all-time record closing highs for the KFX index but dealers foresaw that prices would hold at their lower level.
"The Danish stock market has slipped a little today along with other European markets. Demand is still good though so we see prices holding tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index lost 1.30 point to close almost one percent down at 130.19.
The KFX December future fell 0.80 point to 130.40 with 198 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Tele Danmark was the day's most traded paper with 150,000 shares changing hands before closing five crowns lower at 291.

Among KFX shares only SAS and Carlsberg bucked the downward trend to end with gains, the former closing 0.50 crown higher at 71.50 and the latter putting on a single crown to finish at 376 in a market unimpressed by a record 1995/96 result announced on Monday.
Banks also suffered setbacks with Den Danske Bank shedding eight crowns to close at 442, rival Unidanmark dropping two crowns to 289 and Jyske Bank finishing two lower also at 428.
